result.title: ProPolar: Progressive Polar Decomposition for Implicit Neural Representations
result.summary: Implicit neural representations (INRs) capture global low-frequency structure during the early stage of training and then refine localized high-frequency details, afterwards. However, standard optimizers are agnostic to the coarse-to-fine learning behavior of INRs. Such optimizers accumulate a gradient matrix in momentum buffer and retain components misaligned with the dominant low-frequency directions in the early stage. We propose a progressively growing rank scheduler and a rank-aware learning-rate scheduler for enhancing a subspace-based momentum optimization, where a momentum matrix is updated within a low-rank subspace. The rank schedule expands the subspace during training, and the scheduler holds the peak learning rate through rank growth so that the added subspace contributes to fine-detail recovery. Experiments on image fitting, single-image super-resolution (SISR), and neural radiance field optimization show that the proposed method improves convergence and peak reconstruction quality over competitive optimizers. The largest gains appear in the high-frequency refinement stage, mirroring the coarse-to-fine progression that the rank schedule targets. A significant study on hyperparameter optimization (HPO) on NeRF further confirms that these gains persist under matched search budgets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ProPolar，为低秩子空间动量优化加入逐步增秩的 rank scheduler 与 rank-aware 学习率调度，以匹配 INR 由粗到细的拟合过程，并在图像拟合、SISR 与 NeRF 优化上验证收敛与重建质量提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 按训练阶段扩展低秩子空间并维持峰值学习率的调度思路，可能为 latent 推理状态的容量随阶段增长与高低频信息分配提供可核查线索；但论文面向 INR 重建，与 VLM 推理无直接联系。
